findings: BTZ_1.tex l.1571 (« the proof of Cauchy-completeness of Proposition prop:abs_max applies as is »): it does not apply as is when M has infinitely many BTZ lines, as already recorded (kb/0217). What closes it here: shrink the spears to summable radii; along a path of Sigma*, replace spear by spear (in order of first entry) the piece from the first entry to the last exit by a rim arc of S-length <= pi R_i (the rim arc length R|dtheta| is independent of tau_Sigma); then a Cauchy sequence of Sigma* either comes arbitrarily close, arbitrarily late, to one cusp (the log r estimate of Lemma 2.8 keeps it in a compact annulus graph), or is pushed off the cusp cores to a sequence Cauchy for the S-length, which converges by the completeness of S. The completeness of S for its own length, which B21's compact case never uses, is what the infinite case consumes.
